QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Performance and Benchmarking_48

question.text: A Category I AIF is in Year 9 of a 10-year life with 90% of investments exited. To evaluate the fund's final performance, the MOST informative metric is:

answer.text: RVPI, because residual value dominates at wind-up.
DPI, because distributions have largely been realised and DPI converges to TVPI at wind-up.
PIC Multiple, because it shows capital deployment efficiency.
Sharpe Ratio, because volatility of unlisted holdings is now low.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 7.3.4.2: 'This [DPI] multiple tells the investors how much money they got back. This is better for evaluating a fund later in its life because there are more distributions to measure against.' At Y9 with 90% exits, DPI is mostly complete and is the hard cash number; RVPI is dwindling and less relevant as a valuation mark. The Trap: RVPI (A) is diminishing and dominated by paper marks at this stage. PIC (C) is fully at 1.0 long ago. Sharpe (D) is unsuitable for private markets (see Q23). Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C, XIX-A test the 'DPI in late life' principle. Cambridge/Preqin quartile tables show DPI as the primary sort column for funds >5 years old.
